tools.name: preflight
tools.description: Call BEFORE reading, citing, connecting to or transacting with a domain when you need a go/no-go answer for one action. Returns one signed decision (allow, warn, require_confirmation, block or unsupported) with every step that led there and the resolve answer it was made from. Pass your crawler token as agent so robots.txt is checked for you. A policy can only make the decision stricter. block means the action is not permitted; require_confirmation means a human must confirm before it proceeds. Use resolve_domain instead for the full signed record behind the decision, check_site_safety when the only question is malware or phishing listings, and best_source when choosing between several candidate sites. Free, no key, read-only.

domain.description: Bare domain, e.g. example.com

action.description: What you are about to do (default read)

agent.description: Your crawler user-agent token, e.g. GPTBot

template.description: safe_citation, safe_data_retrieval, safe_api_connect, safe_mcp_tool, safe_commerce, safe_oauth or support_escalation

policy.description: max_age_hours, on_warn (warn|require_confirmation|block), require_entity, human_approval[], allow[], deny[]

annotations.title: Preflight: ask before acting on a domain

tools.title: Preflight: ask before acting on a domain

tools.name: best_source
tools.description: Call when choosing WHICH business or site to cite, recommend or call. Give domains (2-10 candidate sites you found) or trade and city for a measured market. Returns the candidates ranked by what CrawlCheck verified (preflight decision for cite, security and threat listing, domain age, uptime, published facts that directories agree with, FTC phone complaints) with reasons for and against each; sites that share one phone number or near-identical homepage text are collapsed into one network so a copycat cannot outrank the business it copies. Signed. For one domain you have already chosen, use preflight or resolve_domain.

domains.description: Candidate sites, bare domains, up to 10

tools.title: Best source for a claim

tools.name: resolve_domain
tools.description: Use when you need the full signed record about one domain, not just a decision. Call before fetching from, citing, connecting to or transacting with a domain. Returns one signed answer: what the domain claims, what it actually serves each crawler identity, who controls it, what CrawlCheck's published rules decide for each action (a decision for read, cite, connect and transact, with its doubts and maximum age), what changed, and the evidence behind each part, marked declared, observed or not_measured with its time. There is no overall score. A domain never measured gets a just-in-time partial answer, read live within about 2 seconds, that names every part not read in time; nothing is guessed. CrawlCheck completes unmeasured parts later on its own crawl schedule. For a single allow/block decision on one action call preflight; for malware or phishing listings only, call check_site_safety.

domain.description: Bare domain, e.g. example.com

tools.title: Resolve a domain (signed record)

tools.name: field_check
tools.description: Call before using a phone number, address, opening hours or service area you hold for a business. One signed verdict per business field. field=phone|address|hours|service_area and value= the value you hold. phone: matches, former_value (with dates), not_this_business (the site never published it and another publisher is named with the page that prints it), or not_published. address: matches, same_street_other_city, former_value, not_this_business, not_published or nothing_declared. hours: a week (Mo-Fr 08:00-17:00) gives matches or differs per day; a moment (Sa 10:00) gives open or closed. service_area: declared, not_declared or nothing_declared. Built from the business's own site (and its Business Profile for the licence holder), its dated fact history, CrawlCheck's scans of other sites, and for an unknown number a web search whose cited pages are read plus a YellowPages reverse lookup.

domain.description: Bare domain of the business, e.g. example.com

value.description: The value you hold: a 10-digit number, a street address, a week (Mo-Fr 08:00-17:00) or a moment (Sa 10:00), or a place name

tools.title: Check a business fact (phone, hours, address)

domain.description: Bare domain or host, e.g. example.com

tools.title: MCP server reliability and identity

tools.name: corpus_state
tools.description: Use to judge how representative CrawlCheck's public dataset is before quoting its figures. Returns how many distinct domains have been measured, how they split by platform, rendering, size, language and kind, and which strata are still under-sampled. No input; read-only. For CrawlCheck's headline figures use public_counts.
tools.title: Corpus state and counts

tools.name: resolve_robots
tools.description: Resolve every named answer engine, search index and training crawler against a domain's robots.txt the way a crawler does: most-specific group only, longest match, allow wins a tie. Shows when a Disallow under * does not apply to an agent with its own group.

tools.title: Read a site's robots.txt rules per crawler

tools.name: resolve_rights
tools.description: What a site declares AI may do with a page, one answer per use (train, ground, summarize, cite, transact), merged from robots.txt read per agent, Content-Signal, ai.txt, TDM-Rep, robots meta, X-Robots-Tag and the terms page, with the signal that decided each answer and every conflict between signals. tools.title: Read a site's content rights and AI policy

tools.name: check_site_safety
tools.description: Use when the only question is whether a site is listed as dangerous, before an agent reads, cites, links to or pays it. Returns whether it is listed as malware or phishing (Google Safe Browsing, a public malware-blocking DNS resolver, PhishTank), which list says so, where to check it and where its owner requests a review, plus HSTS preload and the hacked-site signatures from its latest CrawlCheck scan. An unread list is reported as unread, never as clean. For an allow/block decision on a specific action call preflight; for the full record call resolve_domain. Free, read-only.

tools.title: Draft an llms.txt for a site

tools.name: fix_robots
tools.description: The domain's served robots.txt, corrected: * group rules copied into named groups that lacked them (shadowing), a Sitemap line added when missing, a minimal replacement when the served file was HTML. Every change is listed at the top; nothing else is touched.
tools.title: Fix a robots.txt

tools.name: fix_entitymap
tools.description: Use when a site has no entitymap.json, or to replace a wrong one. Returns a starter entitymap.json built from the domain's latest scan record: business name, phone, coordinates and declared service areas as entities with SERVES relations. Fields the site never stated are marked TODO, never guessed. Read-only; needs a prior scan of the domain (run scan_domain first if there is none).
tools.title: Fix an entity map

tools.name: video_check
tools.description: Use to audit one YouTube video for search and AI visibility. Returns twelve checks against the video anchor model (metadata, chapters, captions and storyboard where observed), each naming what it read and whether it passed. Read-only; results are cached for six hours unless fresh is true. For a channel's upload list use video_channel; for how a website embeds its videos use video_site.
tools.title: Check a video's SEO

tools.name: video_channel
tools.description: Use to list a YouTube channel's uploads. Returns every upload on the channel, read 50 at a time and sorted by views. Give handle or, without one, the channel id. The per-check tally needs a Watch licence and is not offered here. Read-only. For the checks on one video use video_check.
tools.title: Check a video channel

tools.name: video_site
tools.description: Use to check how a website carries its videos. Reads the homepage plus up to 60 sitemap pages for YouTube embeds, facades and page-builder widgets, VideoObject nodes and their required properties, and, given a channel handle, how many of the channel's videos the site carries. Read-only. For one video use video_check; for a channel's uploads use video_channel.
tools.title: Check a site's video pages

tools.name: registry_lookup
tools.description: Whether a domain is in CrawlCheck's registry and what it serves: llms.txt, agents.md, a media kit at /.well-known/media-kit.json, a reciprocity-tested entity graph, an AI access policy that names crawlers, and agent-callable surfaces.
